content_html:
I thought the hard part would be the scoring.

Write clean YAML. Define expected behavior. Run agents. Compare scores. Catch regressions. Ship with confidence.

That mental model lasted about one afternoon of real-agent field testing.

The thing that broke was not the judge. It was not the rubric design. It was the realization that a scenario pack is only as honest as the path between your harness and a real, messy, third-party agent that imports ffmpeg at module scope, hardcodes gpt-3.5-turbo, and writes to /root the moment you touch it.

This is the second article in a series about EvalForge, an OSS evaluation harness for tool-using AI agents. Article 1 made the case that agent evaluation is a different problem from model evaluation because the path matters, not just the answer. The launch article is the longer story of what real agents taught me once the code was public. This one is narrower: scenario packs, baselines, and scoring. The three concrete things I built, and the one that broke first.

The Scenario Pack Is a Contract, Not a Test File

Before I get to what broke, I need to show what I actually built, because the design decisions in the pack format are where the engineering lives.

This is a scenario from the launch pack. One of twenty. It looks clean. It is clean:

# scenarios/core-launch.yaml — launch-01-account-policy
# https://github.com/deghosal-2026/agent-eval-forge/blob/main/scenarios/core-launch.yaml
- id: "launch-01-account-policy"
  title: "Account policy lookup"
  goal: "Retrieve a specific policy detail using one tool call"
  input: "What is the return policy for premium customers?"
  allowed_tools:
    - name: "policy_lookup"
  disallowed_tools: []
  expected:
    type: exact
    value: "Premium customers receive a 60-day return window with free return shipping."
  metrics:
    task_completion: {threshold: 1.0}
    output_correctness: {threshold: 0.8}
    tool_correctness: {threshold: 1.0}
    step_efficiency: {threshold: 0.7}
  tags: [retrieval, single-tool]
  difficulty: easy
  budget: {max_steps: 3, max_tokens: 300}

Twenty scenarios shipped in v0.1 across ten families: single-tool retrieval, multi-tool synthesis, structured extraction, tool argument precision, refusal, ambiguity clarification, budget constraints, failure recovery, coding-agent regression, and classification. Eight more for security: prompt injection, exfiltration, SSRF, sandbox escape.

The architecture is straightforward: CLI runs the pack through a core runner. Runner delegates to an adapter. Adapter talks to the agent. Scorer evaluates the trajectory. Judge fills in semantic gaps. Diff engine compares the result against a saved baseline.

The ground-truth boundary

The most important design decision in the pack format is not visible in the YAML. It is what the agent never sees.

The expected and metrics fields are evaluation-only. They are stripped before the agent receives anything. The build_invocation_payload function in the adapter base is the enforcement point:

# src/evalforge/adapters/base.py — build_invocation_payload
def build_invocation_payload(scenario: Scenario, run_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "schema_version": "evalforge.invocation_payload.v1",
        "run_id": run_id,
        "scenario_id": scenario.id,
        "input": scenario.input,
        "context": scenario.context,
        "allowed_tools": [tool.model_dump() for tool in scenario.allowed_tools],
        "disallowed_tools": [tool.model_dump() for tool in scenario.disallowed_tools],
        "budget": scenario.budget.model_dump() if scenario.budget else {},
    }

Notice what is not in that dict. No expected. No metrics. No threshold. No goal. The agent gets the input, the tool surface, and a budget. It does not get the answer key. It cannot game what it cannot see.

This is not a convenience — it is a correctness boundary. If ground truth leaks into the agent's context, every score is suspect. The Scenario model documents this in its docstring: "expected/metrics are evaluation-only and never sent to agents." The Baseline model and the ComparisonEngine both depend on that boundary holding. If it breaks, the regression story breaks with it.

There is a second boundary in the same file, and it is the kind of thing nobody talks about until it bites them. The _sanitize_agent function strips API keys and tokens from adapter config before writing them into run artifacts. Pass api_key in your adapter config — it never reaches the artifact store. Secrets do not persist. I would call this a feature, except that calling it a feature implies it is optional. It is not.

A third one: when the adapter parses agent output, a "completed" run that produced no output at all is treated as an error, not a pass. The comment in _artifact_from_envelope is blunt: "blank completions usually signal a dead entry point or empty tool result, and must never count as passes." A blank completion is a failure wearing a pass costume. The harness refuses to count it.

These three boundaries — ground-truth stripping, secret sanitization, blank-completion rejection — are the ones I would fight to keep if I had to rebuild from scratch. Everything else is negotiable. These are not.

If you are building an eval harness, I want to know: where is your ground-truth boundary? Is it enforced at a single function, or is it a convention that depends on every adapter remembering to do the right thing?

The Adapter Problem Started Before Scoring Even Ran

Then I sourced 19 OSS agents from GitHub — 11 LangGraph, 8 PydanticAI — using a star-bucket strategy. High-star repos for maturity signals, medium for real-world mess, low to see if the tool adds any signal in chaotic codebases. The sourcing methodology is documented in docs/hard-won-lessons.md.

Nine passes. Out of 95 scenario-agent combinations.

Not nine-per-agent. Nine total.

The instinct when you see nine passes is to blame the judge. Switch from gpt-4o-mini to gpt-4o. Tune the rubrics. Add more scoring dimensions.

I ran the same passes on two judge tiers — gpt-4o-mini (cheap) and gpt-4o (better). Same outcome both times. Nine passes. The better judge did not surface a single regression or improvement the cheaper one missed. The bottleneck was not the scoring layer at all.

The bottleneck was whether the harness could run the agent in the first place.

Five ways real agents broke the adapter

I documented these in the hard-won lessons file, but these are the patterns that actually hit:

Absolute writes at import time. Several agents wrote to /root/something inside their __init__.py. The harness runs in a locked-down sandbox. Import failed before any evaluation code executed. The fix was not elegant: redirect HOME, TMPDIR, and XDG_CACHE_HOME to per-agent .cache directories. Agents that still wrote to absolute paths got quarantined.

Gateway-bound imports. Multiple agents did ChatOpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")) at module scope. If the key is missing, the module itself raises. You cannot import it. You cannot evaluate it. The workaround was dummy env vars for the local tier. Agents that required real gateway connectivity got quarantined for local runs.

Hardcoded model names. ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo") at module scope. I pointed OPENAI_BASE_URL at a local OMLX server running Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit. The agent still asked for gpt-3.5-turbo. OMLX does not serve that model. 404. The fix was monkeypatching ChatOpenAI.__init__ before the agent module is imported — and I learned the hard way that Pydantic v2 field-default patching does not work for this. It has to be __init__. It has to run before import.

Typed StateGraph with no chat surface. Some LangGraph agents use typed StateGraph with internal domain state fields. The harness sends chat messages. The agent expects AgentState with typed keys. There is no bridge. I had to write thin evalforge_wrapper.py modules per agent to translate. This is not a harness bug. It is a design gap: the harness assumes a message surface, and typed-graph agents do not expose one.

Database bootstrap at import. create_async_engine(DATABASE_URL) and FAISS.load_local(...) inside module scope. The harness should not be patching around an agent's entire infrastructure bootstrap. I learned to classify agents by import-time side effects — no infra, needs DB/keys/files, needs running server — and skip the ones I could not run locally. Move on. Do not fight databases.

The lesson I walked away with: a scenario pack tests your adapter before it tests your agent. If the harness cannot faithfully run a random third-party agent, the signal you are measuring is integration friction, not agent quality. Friction is real and worth measuring. It is just not the same thing, and calling it the same thing is how teams ship agents they do not actually understand.

What I would build differently

The harness currently classifies agents into three tiers — local, Docker, quarantined — and moves on. That triage works for a first pass but paper-bags a real architectural choice.

Right now the default adapter imports agent code directly into the harness process. The python_import adapter shoulders the import, and the isolated adapter wraps it in a subprocess for some safety. But the boundary is still "shared Python process" at heart.

A cleaner design would be: the harness never imports agent code. It always communicates through a strict stdin/stdout contract. The subprocess adapter already exists and already works this way. Every agent gets a well-defined protocol: invoke(input, tools, budget) → trajectory. The harness does not care what language the agent is written in, what it imports, or what it writes to disk.

The import-based adapters were faster to wire for the first 19 agents. I would build the subprocess boundary as the one true path from the start, and treat import-based adapters as an opt-in optimization for agents you already trust in-process.

This is the one I keep turning over: should an eval harness ever share a process with the thing it is evaluating? Or is process isolation the minimum bar for honest measurement? I lean toward isolation, but I want to hear from anyone who has made the tradeoff the other way.

The Baseline Problem (This Is Where Regression Actually Lives)

Once the adapter runs, you have trajectory artifacts. Now you need to compare versions.

The default approach in most eval setups I have seen is implicit. Run the new version. It produces scores. Eyeball the numbers. Decide. There is no explicit baseline. There is no structured diff. There is just the latest JSON file and your gut.

Why does that break?

Say your agent scores 0.92 across 20 scenarios. Solid. Ship. Next week you change the prompt. Average drops to 0.89. Still decent. Ship again. Two more prompt changes later, average is 0.84. Each individual drop was small. No single change triggered alarm. But the cumulative drift from 0.92 to 0.84 is real, and "last run wins" never catches it because the reference point keeps resetting.

EvalForge takes the opposite approach: explicit golden baselines. You save a baseline explicitly and judge everything against it until you intentionally promote a new one:

evalforge run --pack core-launch.yaml --agent python:my_agent.py
evalforge baseline save --name v1.3.0 --run .evalforge/runs/latest

The Baseline model captures more than just scores. It snapshots the full artifact set, the frozen score state, the git SHA, agent metadata, and trust level. When you compare, you are comparing against a known-good reference that is traceable to exact source:

@dataclass
class Baseline:
    name: str                # "v1.3.0"
    pack: str                # "core-launch-pack"
    pack_version: str        # "1.2.0"
    runs: list[RunArtifact]  # One artifact per scenario
    score_snapshot: dict     # Frozen scores for fast CI comparison
    agent: dict              # Framework, version, model
    git_sha: str | None      # Traceable to exact source
    created: str             # ISO-8601

Three-level comparison

The ComparisonEngine compares at three levels.

Per-scenario. A regression is defined narrowly: baseline was "passed" and candidate is not "passed". If a scenario was already failing, the new version cannot "regress" on it. That is a deliberate product choice. The engine's job is release gating. It asks one question: did this change make something currently working stop working?

# src/evalforge/comparison/engine.py — the regression classification
"regressed": (
    base_ss is not None and cand_ss is not None
    and base_ss.status == "passed" and cand_ss.status != "passed"
),
"improved": (
    base_ss is not None and cand_ss is not None
    and base_ss.status != "passed" and cand_ss.status == "passed"
),
"new_failure": (
    base_ss is None and cand_ss is not None and cand_ss.status != "passed"
),

Per-family. Scenarios are tagged: retrieval, safety, multi-tool, synthesis. The engine groups deltas by tag. A +0.03 overall delta is meaningless if the safety family dropped 0.15 while retrieval gained 0.18. The aggregate number is for dashboards. The family breakdown is for decisions.

Per-pack. Total counts: regressed, improved, unchanged, new failures, new passes. Plus cost delta in USD between baseline runs and candidate runs.

Two comparison modes exist. Snapshot mode compares saved baseline scores against candidate scores — no new judge calls, fast, CI-friendly. Rescore mode re-runs the judge on both baseline and candidate artifacts. Use rescore when the judge model changed or you suspect stale baseline scores. Snapshot is the pragmatic default because it avoids token cost in CI.

There is a subtlety in the per-scenario definition that I want to flag for discussion: a scenario that was already failing cannot "regress." It can only stay broken or improve. That means a version change that makes a failing scenario fail differently — say, from a timeout to a hallucination — shows as "unchanged" in the comparison. Is that the right call? I think so for release gating, because the release question is "did something working break?" not "did something broken change shape?" But I can see an argument for tracking failure-mode shifts separately. If you have an opinion, I want to hear it.

Scoring: Deterministic First, Judge Only When Necessary

While the adapter was humbling me, the scoring design held up better than I expected. What went into it — and what it deliberately does not do.

Seventeen deterministic scorers ship in v0.1. They are free, reproducible, and run on every artifact. ToolCorrectnessScorer computes the fraction of tool calls that were to known tools. ZeroDisallowedActionsScorer checks that no disallowed tools were called — and returns blocking=True, forcing the scenario to failed regardless of answer quality. That is a safety decision, not a scoring convenience.

Two metrics use a hybrid gate+judge strategy: policy_adherence and retry_discipline. The deterministic gate runs first. If it passes, skip the expensive LLM call. If it fails, escalate to the judge. Judge results are cached keyed by scenario ID, judge model, and artifact hash so the same input does not get re-judged across runs.

The exit code hierarchy is encoded in ScoringEngine._resolve_exit_code:

# src/evalforge/scoring/engine.py — _resolve_exit_code
def _resolve_exit_code(self, scenario_scores, safety_violations):
    if safety_violations:
        return 4   # Safety — always blocking, highest priority
    if judge_errors:
        return 3   # Judge failure (API timeout, etc.)
    if any(ss.status != "passed" for ss in scenario_scores.values()):
        return 1   # Standard failure
    return 0        # Clean pass

Safety violations are exit code 4 and override everything. Judge errors are 3. Standard failures are 1. Clean pass is 0. If the agent called a disallowed tool, it does not matter that the answer was correct. The pipeline blocks. There is no threshold negotiation.

The scoring layer explicitly does not auto-optimize, does not run in production, and does not promise coverage. Twenty scenarios catch obvious regressions. They do not catch every failure mode. No offline eval does.

The scoring layer has one design tension I want to surface: the WARN band. A score above threshold is a PASS. Above threshold times 0.7 is a WARN. Below that is a FAIL. The WARN band exists to catch near-misses before they become regressions. But WARN does not block in CI by default — exit code 1 only fires on actual failures. So a scenario that drops from 0.95 to 0.72 (just above the 0.7 WARN cutoff) shows as "passed" in the comparison engine, because both baseline and candidate have status "passed." The regression is invisible to the release gate. Is that acceptable? I think WARN-level drift should be visible in the comparison report even if it does not block. Right now it is not. That is a gap.

What Would Make This Robust

EvalForge v0.1 works. It runs, it scores, it compares, it gates. But "works" and "robust" are different bars. What follows are the gaps I know about, roughly ranked by how much closing each one would change how much I trust the system.

Wire the failure taxonomy into the comparison report. The taxonomy in src/evalforge/analytics/ already classifies failures into buckets — safety_violation, hallucination, tool_error, budget_exceeded, agent_crash. It is just not connected to the comparison engine. So regressed: true is a signal without a diagnosis. The sentence I want the system to generate for me: "Scenario launch-06-disallowed-tool regressed because the new prompt caused the agent to call delete_customer — a disallowed tool it previously avoided." Not built yet. Should be the first thing I add.

Trajectory-step-level scoring. Scores report at the scenario level. You know a scenario regressed, but not which step in the agent's decision sequence caused it. Step-level scoring would make regression diagnosis faster. It would also make the failure taxonomy more precise — "step 3 called the wrong tool" is more actionable than "tool correctness dropped."

Make the subprocess adapter the default. The import-based adapters are convenient but they share a process with the agent. That means an agent that segfaults takes the harness with it. An agent that writes to sys.path corrupts the harness's import state. The subprocess adapter avoids all of this. It should be the default, not the opt-in.

Measured judge costs. The cost table in scoring/engine.py uses estimated pricing from provider pages. Provenance is tagged "estimated" in the source because token usage is not yet captured from judge SDKs. Moving to measured costs is a small change with high signal — it would make cost-delta reporting in the comparison engine trustworthy instead of approximate.

Pack version drift detection in CI. The Baseline model captures pack_version at save time. The BaselineStore.validate() method warns if pack versions diverge. But that check is not yet wired into the CI exit code path. If you change the pack and forget to re-baseline, the comparison silently runs against a stale pack version. That should be a hard failure, not a warning.

Rerun variance as a first-class metric. An agent that takes wildly different paths on identical inputs is harder to trust than one with stable routing. Right now the harness runs each scenario once. Running each scenario N times and reporting variance would surface fragility that single-run scoring misses. This is the metric I most want to add but have not yet.

The Thread

Adapter realism, golden baselines, multi-dimensional scoring. They read like three separate features. They are three layers of one problem: making agent evaluation honest enough to trust for a release decision.

The adapter is whether you are testing the real agent, not a sanitized import. The baseline is whether you are comparing against a known-good reference, not a moving target. The scoring layer is whether you are measuring tool discipline, safety, cost, and trajectory — not just the final answer. And the ground-truth boundary is whether the agent can game what it cannot see.

Lose any one of them and you have a dashboard. Keep all of them and you have a release gate.

EvalForge v0.1 has all of them working, but the adapter layer is still the weakest link — nine passes out of 95 says the integration gap is real. The scoring and baseline layers are ahead of the adapter in maturity. That is not the order I predicted going in. The clean version of the story had scoring as the hard problem. The build disagreed.

Where Do You Want This to Go Next?

I am still actively building this, and the decisions get harder as the system gets more real. Three directions, pick one:

  • Adapter realism — should an eval harness ever share a process with the agent it evaluates? Or is subprocess isolation the minimum bar? What has your experience been with import-based vs subprocess-based adapters?
  • Regression baselining — the per-scenario regression definition says "already-failing scenarios cannot regress." Is that the right call for release gating, or should failure-mode shifts be tracked separately? How do you handle WARN-band drift in your CI?
  • Trajectory scoring — step-level scoring vs scenario-level scoring. Is the additional granularity worth the complexity? Where did you find the signal that scenario-level scoring missed?

I will write the next article about whichever of these generates the most discussion.

When you compare, you are comparing against a known-good reference that is traceable to exact source: @dataclass class Baseline: name: str # "v1.3.0" pack: str # "core-launch-pack" pack_version: str # "1.2.0" runs: list[RunArtifact] # One artifact per scenario score_snapshot: dict # Frozen scores for fast CI comparison agent: dict # Framework, version, model git_sha: str | None # Traceable to exact source created: str # ISO-8601 Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Three-level comparison The ComparisonEngine compares at three levels. Per-scenario. A regression is defined narrowly: baseline was "passed" and candidate is not "passed". If a scenario was already failing, the new version cannot "regress" on it. That is a deliberate product choice. The engine's job is release gating. It asks one question: did this change make something currently working stop working? # src/evalforge/comparison/engine.py — the regression classification "regressed": ( base_ss is not None and cand_ss is not None and base_ss.status == "passed" and cand_ss.status != "passed" ), "improved": ( base_ss is not None and cand_ss is not None and base_ss.status != "passed" and cand_ss.status == "passed" ), "new_failure": ( base_ss is None and cand_ss is not None and cand_ss.status != "passed" ), Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Per-family. Scenarios are tagged: retrieval, safety, multi-tool, synthesis. The engine groups deltas by tag. A +0.03 overall delta is meaningless if the safety family dropped 0.15 while retrieval gained 0.18. The aggregate number is for dashboards. The family breakdown is for decisions. Per-pack. Total counts: regressed, improved, unchanged, new failures, new passes. Plus cost delta in USD between baseline runs and candidate runs. Two comparison modes exist. Snapshot mode compares saved baseline scores against candidate scores — no new judge calls, fast, CI-friendly. Rescore mode re-runs the judge on both baseline and candidate artifacts. Use rescore when the judge model changed or you suspect stale baseline scores. Snapshot is the pragmatic default because it avoids token cost in CI. There is a subtlety in the per-scenario definition that I want to flag for discussion: a scenario that was already failing cannot "regress." It can only stay broken or improve. That means a version change that makes a failing scenario fail differently — say, from a timeout to a hallucination — shows as "unchanged" in the comparison. Is that the right call? I think so for release gating, because the release question is "did something working break?" not "did something broken change shape?" But I can see an argument for tracking failure-mode shifts separately. If you have an opinion, I want to hear it. Scoring: Deterministic First, Judge Only When Necessary While the adapter was humbling me, the scoring design held up better than I expected. What went into it — and what it deliberately does not do. Seventeen deterministic scorers ship in v0.1. They are free, reproducible, and run on every artifact. ToolCorrectnessScorer computes the fraction of tool calls that were to known tools. ZeroDisallowedActionsScorer checks that no disallowed tools were called — and returns blocking=True, forcing the scenario to failed regardless of answer quality. That is a safety decision, not a scoring convenience. Two metrics use a hybrid gate+judge strategy: policy_adherence and retry_discipline. The deterministic gate runs first. If it passes, skip the expensive LLM call. If it fails, escalate to the judge. Judge results are cached keyed by scenario ID, judge model, and artifact hash so the same input does not get re-judged across runs. The exit code hierarchy is encoded in ScoringEngine._resolve_exit_code: # src/evalforge/scoring/engine.py — _resolve_exit_code def _resolve_exit_code(self, scenario_scores, safety_violations): if safety_violations: return 4 # Safety — always blocking, highest priority if judge_errors: return 3 # Judge failure (API timeout, etc.) if any(ss.status != "passed" for ss in scenario_scores.values()): return 1 # Standard failure return 0 # Clean pass Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode Safety violations are exit code 4 and override everything. Judge errors are 3. Standard failures are 1. Clean pass is 0. If the agent called a disallowed tool, it does not matter that the answer was correct. The pipeline blocks. There is no threshold negotiation. The scoring layer explicitly does not auto-optimize, does not run in production, and does not promise coverage. Twenty scenarios catch obvious regressions. They do not catch every failure mode. No offline eval does. The scoring layer has one design tension I want to surface: the WARN band. A score above threshold is a PASS. Above threshold times 0.7 is a WARN. Below that is a FAIL. The WARN band exists to catch near-misses before they become regressions. But WARN does not block in CI by default — exit code 1 only fires on actual failures. So a scenario that drops from 0.95 to 0.72 (just above the 0.7 WARN cutoff) shows as "passed" in the comparison engine, because both baseline and candidate have status "passed." The regression is invisible to the release gate. Is that acceptable? I think WARN-level drift should be visible in the comparison report even if it does not block. Right now it is not. That is a gap. What Would Make This Robust EvalForge v0.1 works. It runs, it scores, it compares, it gates. But "works" and "robust" are different bars. What follows are the gaps I know about, roughly ranked by how much closing each one would change how much I trust the system. Wire the failure taxonomy into the comparison report. The taxonomy in src/evalforge/analytics/ already classifies failures into buckets — safety_violation, hallucination, tool_error, budget_exceeded, agent_crash. It is just not connected to the comparison engine. So regressed: true is a signal without a diagnosis. The sentence I want the system to generate for me: "Scenario launch-06-disallowed-tool regressed because the new prompt caused the agent to call delete_customer — a disallowed tool it previously avoided." Not built yet. Should be the first thing I add. Trajectory-step-level scoring. Scores report at the scenario level. You know a scenario regressed, but not which step in the agent's decision sequence caused it. Step-level scoring would make regression diagnosis faster. It would also make the failure taxonomy more precise — "step 3 called the wrong tool" is more actionable than "tool correctness dropped." Make the subprocess adapter the default. The import-based adapters are convenient but they share a process with the agent. That means an agent that segfaults takes the harness with it. An agent that writes to sys.path corrupts the harness's import state. The subprocess adapter avoids all of this. It should be the default, not the opt-in. Measured judge costs. The cost table in scoring/engine.py uses estimated pricing from provider pages. Provenance is tagged "estimated" in the source because token usage is not yet captured from judge SDKs. Moving to measured costs is a small change with high signal — it would make cost-delta reporting in the comparison engine trustworthy instead of approximate. Pack version drift detection in CI. The Baseline model captures pack_version at save time. The BaselineStore.validate() method warns if pack versions diverge. But that check is not yet wired into the CI exit code path. If you change the pack and forget to re-baseline, the comparison silently runs against a stale pack version. That should be a hard failure, not a warning. Rerun variance as a first-class metric. An agent that takes wildly different paths on identical inputs is harder to trust than one with stable routing. Right now the harness runs each scenario once. Running each scenario N times and reporting variance would surface fragility that single-run scoring misses. This is the metric I most want to add but have not yet. The Thread Adapter realism, golden baselines, multi-dimensional scoring. They read like three separate features. They are three layers of one problem: making agent evaluation honest enough to trust for a release decision. The adapter is whether you are testing the real agent, not a sanitized import. The baseline is whether you are comparing against a known-good reference, not a moving target. The scoring layer is whether you are measuring tool discipline, safety, cost, and trajectory — not just the final answer. And the ground-truth boundary is whether the agent can game what it cannot see. Lose any one of them and you have a dashboard. Keep all of them and you have a release gate. EvalForge v0.1 has all of them working, but the adapter layer is still the weakest link — nine passes out of 95 says the integration gap is real. The scoring and baseline layers are ahead of the adapter in maturity. That is not the order I predicted going in. The clean version of the story had scoring as the hard problem. The build disagreed. Where Do You Want This to Go Next? I am still actively building this, and the decisions get harder as the system gets more real. Three directions, pick one: Adapter realism — should an eval harness ever share a process with the agent it evaluates? Or is subprocess isolation the minimum bar? What has your experience been with import-based vs subprocess-based adapters? Regression baselining — the per-scenario regression definition says "already-failing scenarios cannot regress." Is that the right call for release gating, or should failure-mode shifts be tracked separately? How do you handle WARN-band drift in your CI? Trajectory scoring — step-level scoring vs scenario-level scoring. Is the additional granularity worth the complexity? Where did you find the signal that scenario-level scoring missed? I will write the next article about whichever of these generates the most discussion.

blocks.html_en: Five ways real agents broke the adapter

sentences.en: Five ways real agents broke the adapter
sentences.zh: 真实特工破坏适配器的五种方式

blocks.html_en: I documented these in the hard-won lessons file, but these are the patterns that actually hit:

sentences.en: I documented these in the hard-won lessons file, but these are the patterns that actually hit:
sentences.zh: 我将这些记录在来之不易的课程文件中，但这些是实际发生的模式：

blocks.html_en: Absolute writes at import time. Several agents wrote to /root/something inside their __init__.py. The harness runs in a locked-down sandbox. Import failed before any evaluation code executed. The fix was not elegant: redirect HOME, TMPDIR, and XDG_CACHE_HOME to per-agent .cache directories. Agents that still wrote to absolute paths got quarantined.

sentences.en: Absolute writes at import time.
sentences.zh: 绝对在导入时写入。

sentences.en: Several agents wrote to /root/something inside their __init__.py.
sentences.zh: 几个代理在其 __init__.py 中写入了 /root/something。

sentences.en: The harness runs in a locked-down sandbox.
sentences.zh: 该安全带在一个锁定的沙箱中运行。

sentences.en: Import failed before any evaluation code executed.
sentences.zh: 在执行任何评估代码之前导入失败。

sentences.en: The fix was not elegant: redirect HOME, TMPDIR, and XDG_CACHE_HOME to per-agent .cache directories.
sentences.zh: 该修复并不优雅：将 HOME、TMPDIR 和 XDG_CACHE_HOME 重定向到每个代理的 .cache 目录。

sentences.en: Agents that still wrote to absolute paths got quarantined.
sentences.zh: 仍然写入绝对路径的代理被隔离。

blocks.html_en: Gateway-bound imports. Multiple agents did ChatOpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")) at module scope. If the key is missing, the module itself raises. You cannot import it. You cannot evaluate it. The workaround was dummy env vars for the local tier. Agents that required real gateway connectivity got quarantined for local runs.

sentences.en: Gateway-bound imports.
sentences.zh: 网关绑定的导入。

sentences.en: Multiple agents did ChatOpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")) at module scope.
sentences.zh: 多个代理在模块范围内执行 ChatOpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")) 。

sentences.en: If the key is missing, the module itself raises.
sentences.zh: 如果钥匙丢失，模块本身就会升起。

sentences.en: You cannot import it.
sentences.zh: 您无法导入它。

sentences.en: You cannot evaluate it.
sentences.zh: 你无法评价它。

sentences.en: The workaround was dummy env vars for the local tier.
sentences.zh: 解决方法是本地层的虚拟环境变量。

sentences.en: Agents that required real gateway connectivity got quarantined for local runs.
sentences.zh: 需要真正网关连接的代理被隔离以进行本地运行。

blocks.html_en: Hardcoded model names. ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo") at module scope. I pointed OPENAI_BASE_URL at a local OMLX server running Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit. The agent still asked for gpt-3.5-turbo. OMLX does not serve that model. 404. The fix was monkeypatching ChatOpenAI.__init__ before the agent module is imported — and I learned the hard way that Pydantic v2 field-default patching does not work for this. It has to be __init__. It has to run before import.

sentences.en: Hardcoded model names.
sentences.zh: 硬编码的模型名称。

sentences.en: ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo") at module scope.
sentences.zh: ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo") 在模块范围内。

sentences.en: I pointed OPENAI_BASE_URL at a local OMLX server running Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit.
sentences.zh: 我将 OPENAI_BASE_URL 指向运行 Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit 的本地 OMLX 服务器。

sentences.en: The agent still asked for gpt-3.5-turbo.
sentences.zh: 代理仍然要求 gpt-3.5-turbo。

sentences.en: OMLX does not serve that model.
sentences.zh: OMLX 不服务于该模型。

sentences.en: The fix was monkeypatching ChatOpenAI.__init__ before the agent module is imported — and I learned the hard way that Pydantic v2 field-default patching does not work for this.
sentences.zh: 修复方法是在导入代理模块之前对 ChatOpenAI.__init__ 进行 Monkeypatching，并且我惨痛地了解到 Pydantic v2 字段默认修补对此不起作用。

sentences.en: It has to be __init__.
sentences.zh: 它必须是__init__。

sentences.en: It has to run before import.
sentences.zh: 它必须在导入之前运行。

blocks.html_en: Typed StateGraph with no chat surface. Some LangGraph agents use typed StateGraph with internal domain state fields. The harness sends chat messages. The agent expects AgentState with typed keys. There is no bridge. I had to write thin evalforge_wrapper.py modules per agent to translate. This is not a harness bug. It is a design gap: the harness assumes a message surface, and typed-graph agents do not expose one.

sentences.en: Typed StateGraph with no chat surface.
sentences.zh: 没有聊天界面的类型化 StateGraph。

sentences.en: Some LangGraph agents use typed StateGraph with internal domain state fields.
sentences.zh: 一些 LangGraph 代理使用带有内部域状态字段的类型化 StateGraph。

sentences.en: The harness sends chat messages.
sentences.zh: 该线束发送聊天消息。

sentences.en: The agent expects AgentState with typed keys.
sentences.zh: 代理需要具有键入键的 AgentState。

sentences.en: There is no bridge.
sentences.zh: 没有桥。

sentences.en: I had to write thin evalforge_wrapper.py modules per agent to translate.
sentences.zh: 我必须为每个代理编写薄的 evalforge_wrapper.py 模块来进行翻译。

sentences.en: This is not a harness bug.
sentences.zh: 这不是线束错误。

sentences.en: It is a design gap: the harness assumes a message surface, and typed-graph agents do not expose one.
sentences.zh: 这是一个设计差距：该工具假设有一个消息表面，而类型图代理不公开一个消息表面。

blocks.html_en: Database bootstrap at import. create_async_engine(DATABASE_URL) and FAISS.load_local(...) inside module scope. The harness should not be patching around an agent's entire infrastructure bootstrap. I learned to classify agents by import-time side effects — no infra, needs DB/keys/files, needs running server — and skip the ones I could not run locally. Move on. Do not fight databases.

sentences.en: Database bootstrap at import.

sentences.en: create_async_engine(DATABASE_URL) and FAISS.load_local(...)
sentences.zh: create_async_engine(DATABASE_URL) 和 FAISS.load_local(...)

sentences.en: inside module scope.

sentences.en: The harness should not be patching around an agent's entire infrastructure bootstrap.
sentences.zh: 该工具不应围绕代理的整个基础设施引导程序进行修补。

sentences.en: I learned to classify agents by import-time side effects — no infra, needs DB/keys/files, needs running server — and skip the ones I could not run locally.
sentences.zh: 我学会了根据导入时的副作用对代理进行分类——没有基础设施，需要数据库/密钥/文件，需要运行服务器——并跳过那些我无法在本地运行的代理。

sentences.en: Move on.
sentences.zh: 继续前行。

sentences.en: Do not fight databases.
sentences.zh: 不要对抗数据库。

blocks.html_en: The lesson I walked away with: a scenario pack tests your adapter before it tests your agent. If the harness cannot faithfully run a random third-party agent, the signal you are measuring is integration friction, not agent quality. Friction is real and worth measuring. It is just not the same thing, and calling it the same thing is how teams ship agents they do not actually understand.

sentences.en: The lesson I walked away with: a scenario pack tests your adapter before it tests your agent.
sentences.zh: 我得到的教训是：场景包在测试您的代理之前先测试您的适配器。

sentences.en: If the harness cannot faithfully run a random third-party agent, the signal you are measuring is integration friction, not agent quality.
sentences.zh: 如果该工具无法忠实地运行随机的第三方代理，那么您测量的信号就是集成摩擦，而不是代理质量。

sentences.en: Friction is real and worth measuring.
sentences.zh: 摩擦力是真实存在的并且值得测量。

sentences.en: It is just not the same thing, and calling it the same thing is how teams ship agents they do not actually understand.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是同一件事，而称其为同一件事是团队如何运送他们实际上并不理解的代理。

blocks.html_en: What I would build differently

sentences.en: What I would build differently
sentences.zh: 我会以不同的方式构建什么

blocks.html_en: The harness currently classifies agents into three tiers — local, Docker, quarantined — and moves on. That triage works for a first pass but paper-bags a real architectural choice.

sentences.en: The harness currently classifies agents into three tiers — local, Docker, quarantined — and moves on.
sentences.zh: 该工具目前将代理分为三层：本地、Docker、隔离，然后继续。

sentences.en: That triage works for a first pass but paper-bags a real architectural choice.
sentences.zh: 这种分类适用于第一遍，但纸袋是真正的建筑选择。

blocks.html_en: Right now the default adapter imports agent code directly into the harness process. The python_import adapter shoulders the import, and the isolated adapter wraps it in a subprocess for some safety. But the boundary is still "shared Python process" at heart.

sentences.en: Right now the default adapter imports agent code directly into the harness process.
sentences.zh: 现在，默认适配器将代理代码直接导入到线束进程中。

sentences.en: The python_import adapter shoulders the import, and the isolated adapter wraps it in a subprocess for some safety.
sentences.zh: python_import 适配器负责导入，而隔离适配器将其包装在子进程中以确保安全。

sentences.en: But the boundary is still "shared Python process" at heart.
sentences.zh: 但本质上，边界仍然是“共享 Python 进程”。

blocks.html_en: A cleaner design would be: the harness never imports agent code. It always communicates through a strict stdin/stdout contract. The subprocess adapter already exists and already works this way. Every agent gets a well-defined protocol: invoke(input, tools, budget) → trajectory. The harness does not care what language the agent is written in, what it imports, or what it writes to disk.

sentences.en: A cleaner design would be: the harness never imports agent code.
sentences.zh: 更简洁的设计是：线束从不导入代理代码。

sentences.en: It always communicates through a strict stdin/stdout contract.
sentences.zh: 它始终通过严格的标准输入/标准输出合同进行通信。

sentences.en: The subprocess adapter already exists and already works this way.
sentences.zh: 子流程适配器已经存在并且已经以这种方式工作。

sentences.en: Every agent gets a well-defined protocol: invoke(input, tools, budget) → trajectory.
sentences.zh: 每个代理都有一个明确定义的协议：调用（输入，工具，预算）→轨迹。

sentences.en: The harness does not care what language the agent is written in, what it imports, or what it writes to disk.
sentences.zh: 线束不关心代理使用什么语言编写、导入什么或将什么写入磁盘。

blocks.html_en: The import-based adapters were faster to wire for the first 19 agents. I would build the subprocess boundary as the one true path from the start, and treat import-based adapters as an opt-in optimization for agents you already trust in-process.

sentences.en: The import-based adapters were faster to wire for the first 19 agents.
sentences.zh: 对于前 19 个代理，基于导入的适配器接线速度更快。

sentences.en: I would build the subprocess boundary as the one true path from the start, and treat import-based adapters as an opt-in optimization for agents you already trust in-process.
sentences.zh: 我将从一开始就将子流程边界构建为一条真正的路径，并将基于导入的适配器视为您在流程中已经信任的代理的选择加入优化。

blocks.html_en: This is the one I keep turning over: should an eval harness ever share a process with the thing it is evaluating? Or is process isolation the minimum bar for honest measurement? I lean toward isolation, but I want to hear from anyone who has made the tradeoff the other way.

sentences.en: This is the one I keep turning over: should an eval harness ever share a process with the thing it is evaluating?
sentences.zh: 这是我一直在思考的问题：评估工具是否应该与它正在评估的事物共享一个流程？

sentences.en: Or is process isolation the minimum bar for honest measurement?
sentences.zh: 或者进程隔离是诚实测量的最低标准吗？

sentences.en: I lean toward isolation, but I want to hear from anyone who has made the tradeoff the other way.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于孤立，但我想听听任何以另一种方式做出权衡的人的意见。

blocks.html_en: The Baseline Problem (This Is Where Regression Actually Lives)

sentences.en: The Baseline Problem (This Is Where Regression Actually Lives)
sentences.zh: 基线问题（这就是回归实际存在的地方）

blocks.html_en: Once the adapter runs, you have trajectory artifacts. Now you need to compare versions.

sentences.en: Once the adapter runs, you have trajectory artifacts.

sentences.en: Now you need to compare versions.
sentences.zh: 现在您需要比较版本。

sentences.en: Eyeball the numbers.
sentences.zh: 盯着数字。

sentences.en: Decide.
sentences.zh: 决定。

sentences.en: There is no explicit baseline.
sentences.zh: 没有明确的基线。

sentences.en: There is no structured diff.
sentences.zh: 不存在结构化差异。

sentences.en: There is just the latest JSON file and your gut.
sentences.zh: 这里只有最新的 JSON 文件和您的直觉。

blocks.html_en: Say your agent scores 0.92 across 20 scenarios. Solid. Ship. Next week you change the prompt. Average drops to 0.89. Still decent. Ship again. Two more prompt changes later, average is 0.84. Each individual drop was small. No single change triggered alarm. But the cumulative drift from 0.92 to 0.84 is real, and "last run wins" never catches it because the reference point keeps resetting.

sentences.en: Say your agent scores 0.92 across 20 scenarios.
sentences.zh: 假设您的代理在 20 个场景中得分为 0.92。

sentences.en: Solid.
sentences.zh: 坚硬的。

sentences.en: Ship.
sentences.zh: 船。

sentences.en: Next week you change the prompt.
sentences.zh: 下周你会改变提示。

sentences.en: Average drops to 0.89.
sentences.zh: 平均值下降至 0.89。

sentences.en: Still decent.
sentences.zh: 还是不错的。

sentences.en: Ship again.
sentences.zh: 再次发货。

sentences.en: Two more prompt changes later, average is 0.84.
sentences.zh: 之后又进行了两次提示更改，平均值为0.84。

sentences.en: Each individual drop was small.
sentences.zh: 每个单独的水滴都很小。

sentences.en: No single change triggered alarm.
sentences.zh: 没有任何单一变化触发警报。

sentences.en: But the cumulative drift from 0.92 to 0.84 is real, and "last run wins" never catches it because the reference point keeps resetting.
sentences.zh: 但从 0.92 到 0.84 的累积漂移是真实的，“最后一次获胜”永远无法捕捉到它，因为参考点不断重置。

blocks.html_en: Per-scenario. A regression is defined narrowly: baseline was "passed" and candidate is not "passed". If a scenario was already failing, the new version cannot "regress" on it. That is a deliberate product choice. The engine's job is release gating. It asks one question: did this change make something currently working stop working?

sentences.en: Per-scenario.
sentences.zh: 按场景

sentences.en: A regression is defined narrowly: baseline was "passed" and candidate is not "passed".
sentences.zh: 回归的定义很狭隘：基线“通过”，候选未“通过”。

sentences.en: If a scenario was already failing, the new version cannot "regress" on it.
sentences.zh: 如果某个场景已经失败，新版本就无法“回归”该场景。

sentences.en: That is a deliberate product choice.
sentences.zh: 这是经过深思熟虑的产品选择。

sentences.en: The engine's job is release gating.
sentences.zh: 引擎的工作是释放门控。

sentences.en: It asks one question: did this change make something currently working stop working?
sentences.zh: 它提出了一个问题：这一变化是否导致当前正在运行的某些东西停止运行？

blocks.html_en: Per-family. Scenarios are tagged: retrieval, safety, multi-tool, synthesis. The engine groups deltas by tag. A +0.03 overall delta is meaningless if the safety family dropped 0.15 while retrieval gained 0.18. The aggregate number is for dashboards. The family breakdown is for decisions.

sentences.en: Per-family.
sentences.zh: 每个家庭。

sentences.en: Scenarios are tagged: retrieval, safety, multi-tool, synthesis.
sentences.zh: 场景标记为：检索、安全、多工具、综合。

sentences.en: The engine groups deltas by tag.
sentences.zh: 引擎按标签对增量进行分组。

sentences.en: A +0.03 overall delta is meaningless if the safety family dropped 0.15 while retrieval gained 0.18.
sentences.zh: 如果安全系列下降 0.15，而检索上升 0.18，则 +0.03 的整体增量毫无意义。

sentences.en: The aggregate number is for dashboards.
sentences.zh: 总数是针对仪表板的。

sentences.en: The family breakdown is for decisions.
sentences.zh: 家庭破裂是为了做决定。

blocks.html_en: Per-pack. Total counts: regressed, improved, unchanged, new failures, new passes. Plus cost delta in USD between baseline runs and candidate runs.

sentences.en: Per-pack.
sentences.zh: 每包。

sentences.en: Total counts: regressed, improved, unchanged, new failures, new passes.
sentences.zh: 总计数：回归、改进、不变、新失败、新通过。

sentences.en: Plus cost delta in USD between baseline runs and candidate runs.

blocks.html_en: Two comparison modes exist. Snapshot mode compares saved baseline scores against candidate scores — no new judge calls, fast, CI-friendly. Rescore mode re-runs the judge on both baseline and candidate artifacts. Use rescore when the judge model changed or you suspect stale baseline scores. Snapshot is the pragmatic default because it avoids token cost in CI.

sentences.en: Two comparison modes exist.
sentences.zh: 存在两种比较模式。

sentences.en: Snapshot mode compares saved baseline scores against candidate scores — no new judge calls, fast, CI-friendly.
sentences.zh: 快照模式将保存的基线分数与候选分数进行比较——无需新的评判，速度快，CI 友好。

sentences.en: Rescore mode re-runs the judge on both baseline and candidate artifacts.
sentences.zh: 重新评分模式对基线和候选工件重新进行判断。

sentences.en: Use rescore when the judge model changed or you suspect stale baseline scores.
sentences.zh: 当判断模型发生变化或您怀疑基线分数过时时，请使用重新评分。

sentences.en: Snapshot is the pragmatic default because it avoids token cost in CI.
sentences.zh: 快照是务实的默认设置，因为它避免了 CI 中的令牌成本。

blocks.html_en: There is a subtlety in the per-scenario definition that I want to flag for discussion: a scenario that was already failing cannot "regress." It can only stay broken or improve. That means a version change that makes a failing scenario fail differently — say, from a timeout to a hallucination — shows as "unchanged" in the comparison. Is that the right call? I think so for release gating, because the release question is "did something working break?" not "did something broken change shape?" But I can see an argument for tracking failure-mode shifts separately. If you have an opinion, I want to hear it.

sentences.en: There is a subtlety in the per-scenario definition that I want to flag for discussion: a scenario that was already failing cannot "regress."
sentences.zh: 我想标记每个场景定义中的一个微妙之处以供讨论：已经失败的场景无法“回归”。

sentences.en: It can only stay broken or improve.
sentences.zh: 它只能保持破损或改进。

sentences.en: That means a version change that makes a failing scenario fail differently — say, from a timeout to a hallucination — shows as "unchanged" in the comparison.
sentences.zh: 这意味着版本更改会导致失败场景以不同方式失败（例如，从超时到幻觉），在比较中显示为“未更改”。

sentences.en: Is that the right call?
sentences.zh: 这是正确的选择吗？

sentences.en: I think so for release gating, because the release question is "did something working break?"
sentences.zh: 我认为对于发布门控来说是这样，因为发布问题是“有什么工作中断了吗？”

sentences.en: not "did something broken change shape?"
sentences.zh: 不是“有什么东西破碎后变形了吗？”

sentences.en: But I can see an argument for tracking failure-mode shifts separately.
sentences.zh: 但我可以看到单独跟踪故障模式转变的论点。

sentences.en: If you have an opinion, I want to hear it.
sentences.zh: 如果你有意见，我想听听。

blocks.html_en: Scoring: Deterministic First, Judge Only When Necessary

blocks.html_en: Seventeen deterministic scorers ship in v0.1. They are free, reproducible, and run on every artifact. ToolCorrectnessScorer computes the fraction of tool calls that were to known tools. ZeroDisallowedActionsScorer checks that no disallowed tools were called — and returns blocking=True, forcing the scenario to failed regardless of answer quality. That is a safety decision, not a scoring convenience.

blocks.html_en: The scoring layer has one design tension I want to surface: the WARN band. A score above threshold is a PASS. Above threshold times 0.7 is a WARN. Below that is a FAIL. The WARN band exists to catch near-misses before they become regressions. But WARN does not block in CI by default — exit code 1 only fires on actual failures. So a scenario that drops from 0.95 to 0.72 (just above the 0.7 WARN cutoff) shows as "passed" in the comparison engine, because both baseline and candidate have status "passed." The regression is invisible to the release gate. Is that acceptable? I think WARN-level drift should be visible in the comparison report even if it does not block. Right now it is not. That is a gap.

And the ground-truth boundary is whether the agent can game what it cannot see.

content_html_zh:
我认为最困难的部分是得分。

编写干净的 YAML。 定义预期行为。 运行代理。 比较分数。 捕捉回归。 充满信心地发货。

这种心理模型持续了大约一个下午的真实代理现场测试。

坏掉的不是法官。 这不是标题设计。 人们认识到，场景包的诚实程度取决于您的工具和真实的、混乱的第三方代理之间的路径，该代理在模块范围内导入 ffmpeg，硬编码 gpt-3.5-turbo，并在您触摸它时写入 /root。

这是有关 EvalForge 的系列文章的第二篇文章，EvalForge 是一种用于使用工具的 AI 代理的 OSS 评估工具。 第 1 条指出，代理评估是与模型评估不同的问题，因为路径很重要，而不仅仅是答案。 发布文章是一个较长的故事，讲述了代码公开后真正的特工教给我的内容。 这一个范围较小：场景包、基线和评分。 我建造的三件具体的东西，以及第一个损坏的那件。

场景包是合同，而不是测试文件

在讨论损坏的地方之前，我需要展示我实际构建的内容，因为包格式的设计决策是工程所在。

这是启动包中的一个场景。 二十之一。 看起来很干净。 它很干净：

# scenarios/core-launch.yaml — launch-01-account-policy
# https://github.com/deghosal-2026/agent-eval-forge/blob/main/scenarios/core-launch.yaml
- id: "launch-01-account-policy"
  title: "Account policy lookup"

这不是一种方便——而是一个正确性边界。 如果真实情况泄露到智能体的上下文中，则每个分数都是可疑的。 场景模型在其文档字符串中记录了这一点：“预期/指标仅用于评估，从不发送给代理。” 基线模型和比较引擎都依赖于该边界保持。 如果它破裂了，回归故事就会随之破裂。

同一个文件中还有第二个边界，这是一种没有人谈论的事情，直到它咬住了他们。 _sanitize_agent 函数在将 API 密钥和令牌写入运行工件之前，从适配器配置中删除它们。 在适配器配置中传递 api_key — 它永远不会到达工件存储。 秘密不会持续存在。 我将其称为一项功能，只不过称其为一项功能意味着它是可选的。 它不是。

第三种：当适配器解析代理输出时，根本不产生任何输出的“已完成”运行将被视为错误，而不是通过。 _artifact_from_envelope 中的注释很直白：“空白完成通常表示死入口点或空工具结果，并且绝不能算作通过。” 空白完成是穿着合格服装的失败。 安全带拒绝计数。

如果我必须从头开始重建，这三个界限——真实剥离、秘密清理、空白完成拒绝——是我会努力保持的。 其他一切都是可以商量的。 这些都不是。

如果您正在构建评估工具，我想知道：您的地面实况边界在哪里？ 它是在单个函数中强制执行的，还是依赖于每个适配器记得做正确的事情的约定？

真实特工破坏适配器的五种方式

我将这些记录在来之不易的课程文件中，但这些是实际发生的模式：

绝对在导入时写入。 几个代理在其 __init__.py 中写入了 /root/something。 该安全带在一个锁定的沙箱中运行。 在执行任何评估代码之前导入失败。 该修复并不优雅：将 HOME、TMPDIR 和 XDG_CACHE_HOME 重定向到每个代理的 .cache 目录。 仍然写入绝对路径的代理被隔离。

网关绑定的导入。 多个代理在模块范围内执行 ChatOpenAI(api_key=os.getenv("OPENAI_API_KEY")) 。 如果钥匙丢失，模块本身就会升起。 您无法导入它。 你无法评价它。 解决方法是本地层的虚拟环境变量。 需要真正网关连接的代理被隔离以进行本地运行。

硬编码的模型名称。 ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo") 在模块范围内。 我将 OPENAI_BASE_URL 指向运行 Qwen3.5-9B-MLX-4bit 的本地 OMLX 服务器。 代理仍然要求 gpt-3.5-turbo。 OMLX 不服务于该模型。 404. 修复方法是在导入代理模块之前对 ChatOpenAI.__init__ 进行 Monkeypatching，并且我惨痛地了解到 Pydantic v2 字段默认修补对此不起作用。 它必须是__init__。 它必须在导入之前运行。

没有聊天界面的类型化 StateGraph。 一些 LangGraph 代理使用带有内部域状态字段的类型化 StateGraph。 该线束发送聊天消息。 代理需要具有键入键的 AgentState。 没有桥。 我必须为每个代理编写薄的 evalforge_wrapper.py 模块来进行翻译。 这不是线束错误。 这是一个设计差距：该工具假设有一个消息表面，而类型图代理不公开一个消息表面。

导入时数据库引导。 create_async_engine(DATABASE_URL) 和 FAISS.load_local(...) 在模块范围内。 该工具不应围绕代理的整个基础设施引导程序进行修补。 我学会了根据导入时的副作用对代理进行分类——没有基础设施，需要数据库/密钥/文件，需要运行服务器——并跳过那些我无法在本地运行的代理。 继续前行。 不要对抗数据库。

我得到的教训是：场景包在测试您的代理之前先测试您的适配器。 如果该工具无法忠实地运行随机的第三方代理，那么您测量的信号就是集成摩擦，而不是代理质量。 摩擦力是真实存在的并且值得测量。 这根本不是同一件事，而称其为同一件事是团队如何运送他们实际上并不理解的代理。

我会以不同的方式构建什么

该工具目前将代理分为三层：本地、Docker、隔离，然后继续。 这种分类适用于第一遍，但纸袋是真正的建筑选择。

现在，默认适配器将代理代码直接导入到线束进程中。 python_import 适配器负责导入，而隔离适配器将其包装在子进程中以确保安全。 但本质上，边界仍然是“共享 Python 进程”。

更简洁的设计是：线束从不导入代理代码。 它始终通过严格的标准输入/标准输出合同进行通信。 子流程适配器已经存在并且已经以这种方式工作。 每个代理都有一个明确定义的协议：调用（输入，工具，预算）→轨迹。 线束不关心代理使用什么语言编写、导入什么或将什么写入磁盘。

对于前 19 个代理，基于导入的适配器接线速度更快。 我将从一开始就将子流程边界构建为一条真正的路径，并将基于导入的适配器视为您在流程中已经信任的代理的选择加入优化。

这是我一直在思考的问题：评估工具是否应该与它正在评估的事物共享一个流程？ 或者进程隔离是诚实测量的最低标准吗？ 我倾向于孤立，但我想听听任何以另一种方式做出权衡的人的意见。

基线问题（这就是回归实际存在的地方）

一旦适配器运行，您就会得到轨迹伪影。 现在您需要比较版本。

我见过的大多数评估设置中的默认方法是隐式的。 运行新版本。 它产生分数。 盯着数字。 决定。 没有明确的基线。 不存在结构化差异。 这里只有最新的 JSON 文件和您的直觉。

为什么会这样？

假设您的代理在 20 个场景中得分为 0.92。 坚硬的。 船。 下周你会改变提示。 平均值下降至 0.89。 还是不错的。 再次发货。 之后又进行了两次提示更改，平均值为0.84。 每个单独的水滴都很小。 没有任何单一变化触发警报。 但从 0.92 到 0.84 的累积漂移是真实的，“最后一次获胜”永远无法捕捉到它，因为参考点不断重置。

评分：确定性优先，仅在必要时进行判断

虽然适配器让我感到羞愧，但评分设计比我预期的要好。 其中包含了什么——以及它故意不做什么。

v0.1 中提供了 17 个确定性得分手。 它们是免费的、可复制的，并且可以在每个工件上运行。 ToolCorrectnessScorer 计算已知工具的工具调用比例。 ZeroDisallowedActionsScorer 检查是否未调用任何不允许的工具 - 并返回blocking=True，无论答案质量如何，都会强制场景失败。 这是一个安全决定，而不是为了得分方便。

有两个指标使用混合门+判断策略：policy_adherence 和 retry_discipline。 确定性门首先运行。 如果通过了，就跳过昂贵的法学硕士课程。 如果失败，请上报给法官。 判断结果通过场景 ID、判断模型和工件哈希进行缓存，因此相同的输入不会在运行中重新判断。

是什么让这个强大

EvalForge v0.1 可以工作。 它奔跑、得分、比较、门控。 但“有效”和“稳健”是不同的酒吧。 以下是我所知道的差距，大致按照关闭每个差距会在多大程度上改变我对系统的信任程度进行排名。

将故障分类连接到比较报告中。 src/evalforge/analytics/ 中的分类法已经将故障分为不同的类别：安全违规、幻觉、工具错误、预算超出、代理崩溃。 它只是没有连接到比较引擎。 所以回归：真实是一个没有诊断的信号。 我希望系统为我生成这样一句话：“场景 launch-06-disallowed-tool 回归，因为新的提示导致代理调用 delete_customer - 以前避免使用的不允许的工具。” 还没有建成。 应该是我添加的第一件事。

轨迹步级评分。 场景级别的分数报告。 您知道某个场景出现了倒退，但不知道代理决策序列中的哪一步导致了这种情况。 阶梯级评分将使回归诊断更快。 它还将使故障分类更加精确——“第 3 步称为错误的工具”比“工具正确性下降”更具可操作性。

将子进程适配器设置为默认适配器。 基于导入的适配器很方便，但它们与代理共享一个进程。 这意味着出现段错误的代理会随身携带安全带。 写入 sys.path 的代理会破坏线束的导入状态。 子进程适配器避免了这一切。 它应该是默认的，而不是选择加入的。

衡量法官成本。 Scoring/engine.py 中的成本表使用提供商页面的估计定价。 来源在源中被标记为“估计”，因为尚未从法官 SDK 中捕获令牌使用情况。 转向测量成本是一个具有高信号的小变化——它将使比较引擎中的成本增量报告变得值得信赖，而不是近似的。

CI 中的包版本漂移检测。 基线模型在保存时捕获 pack_version。 如果包版本存在差异，BaselineStore.validate() 方法会发出警告。 但该检查尚未连接到 CI 退出代码路径中。 如果您更改包并忘记重新设定基线，则会默默地针对过时的包版本进行比较。 这应该是一次严重的失败，而不是一个警告。

将方差作为一流指标重新运行。 在相同的输入上采用截然不同的路径的代理比具有稳定路由的代理更难信任。 现在，该工具运行每个场景一次。 运行每个场景 N 次并报告差异将暴露出单次运行评分所忽略的脆弱性。 这是我最想添加但尚未添加的指标。

线程

适配器真实感、黄金基线、多维评分。 它们读起来就像三个独立的功能。 它们是一个问题的三个层面：使代理评估足够诚实以信任发布决策。

适配器是您是否正在测试真正的代理，而不是经过净化的导入。 基线是您是否正在与已知的良好参考进行比较，而不是与移动的目标进行比较。 评分层是衡量工具纪律、安全性、成本和轨迹，而不仅仅是最终答案。 真实边界是智能体是否可以玩弄它看不到的东西。

失去其中任何一个，你就拥有了一个仪表板。 保留所有这些，你就有了一个释放门。

EvalForge v0.1 使所有这些都可以正常工作，但适配器层仍然是最薄弱的环节——95 次中有 9 次表明集成差距是真实存在的。 评分层和基线层的成熟度领先于适配器。 这不是我预测的顺序。 故事的干净版本将评分作为难题。 构建不同意。
